newsitem.title: CANADA: MacMillan guilty on three spill charges.
newsitem.headline: MacMillan guilty on three spill charges.

text.p: MacMillan Bloedel Ltd said on Thursday a British Columbia court found it guilty of three environmental charges relating to a chlorine dioxide spill at its pulp mill at Powell River, British Columbia in 1994.
The three charges related to the discharge of waste in violation of provincial law and deposit of a harmful substance in the water, a company spokesman said.
The court will hand down a penalty against the company in September and the maximum punishment would be a C$2.3 million fine, the spokesman said.
The provincial court judge cleared MacMillan of five other charges relating to the company's response to the spill.

On October 17, 1994, a pulp storage tank at the mill failed and fell on nearby chlorine dioxide tanks. The tanks ruptured and released 600,000 liters of chemical. The spill was one of the biggest in the province's history.
